react_result.final_narrative_text: The nine-differential metabolite panel strongly and consistently implicates disruption of pyrimidine metabolism. Four metabolites form the robust core driver set identified across all three analysis paradigms: deoxyuridine (2'-deoxyuridine), uridine 5'-monophosphate, 5,6-dihydrouracil, and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine (ureidopropionic acid). These four achieved FDR = 1.74×10⁻¹⁰ in RaMP multi-DB ORA (the top eight RaMP hits are all pyrimidine-related: pyrimidine catabolism Reactome pathway R-HSA-73621, pyrimidine metabolism WikiPathways WP4022, and KEGG map00240), p = 4.47×10⁻⁶ in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and p = 0.00042 in Mummichog m/z-direct (which additionally captured CDP and deoxyribose 1-phosphate from the same pathway with near-complete 13/14 compound overlap). Methionine sulfoxide, 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid, and spironolactone were not detected in pyrimidine pathway hits and represent treatment-specific changes unrelated to the central pyrimidine signal. The converging evidence across ORA, PSEA, and m/z-direct methods establishes pyrimidine catabolism and salvage as the dominant biological axis perturbed in the treatment condition, with deoxyuridine and dihydrouracil likely reflecting altered thymidylate synthase flux and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase activity.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms—RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct—converged on pyrimidine metabolism as the dominant perturbed axis. RaMP ORA identified Biomarkers for pyrimidine metabolism disorders (WP:WP4584) as the top hit with FDR = 1.74×10⁻¹⁰, capturing four metabolites: 2'-deoxyuridine (MXHRCPNRJAMMIM-SHYZEUOFSA-N), uridine 5'-monophosphate (DJJCXFVJDGTHFX-XVFCMESISA-N), 5,6-dihydrouracil (OIVLITBTBDPEFK-UHFFFAOYSA-N), and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine (JSJWCHRYRHKBBW-UHFFFAOYSA-N). Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621) and Pyrimidine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00240) appeared as rank-0 or rank-1 hits across RaMP and MetaboAnalystR respectively, with the four-molecule set achieving p = 4.47×10⁻⁶ in the KEGG-only PSEA. Mummichog m/z-direct independently recovered pyrimidine metabolism (MUMM:pyrimidine_metabolism, p = 5.04×10⁻⁴) with 13 of 14 pathway compounds matched, including CDP (ZWIADYZPOWUWEW-XVFCMESISA-N) and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (KBDKAJNTYKVSEK-VPENINKCSA-N) that were absent from the ORA input list but detected via mass-matching. Spironolactone (LXMSZDCAJNLERA), 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (DWAKNKKXGALPNW-BYPYZUCNSA-N), and methionine sulfoxide (QEFRNWWLZKMPFJ) did not appear in any pyrimidine-pathway hit across the three tools, indicating they are treatment-specific signals orthogonal to the core pyrimidine enrichment. The convergent evidence across ORA, PSEA, and m/z-direct establishes pyrimidine catabolism and salvage as the primary biological axis perturbed in the treatment condition.

Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621) and Pyrimidine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00240) appeared as rank-0 or rank-1 hits across RaMP and MetaboAnalystR respectively, with the four-molecule set achieving p = 4.47×10⁻⁶ in the KEGG-only PSEA. Mummichog m/z-direct independently recovered pyrimidine metabolism (MUMM:pyrimidine_metabolism, p = 5.04×10⁻⁴) with 13 of 14 pathway compounds matched, including CDP (ZWIADYZPOWUWEW-XVFCMESISA-N) and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (KBDKAJNTYKVSEK-VPENINKCSA-N) that were absent from the ORA input list but detected via mass-matching. Spironolactone (LXMSZDCAJNLERA), 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (DWAKNKKXGALPNW-BYPYZUCNSA-N), and methionine sulfoxide (QEFRNWWLZKMPFJ) did not appear in any pyrimidine-pathway hit across the three tools, indicating they are treatment-specific signals orthogonal to the core pyrimidine enrichment. The convergent evidence across ORA, PSEA, and m/z-direct establishes pyrimidine catabolism and salvage as the primary biological axis perturbed in the treatment condition.
